Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment
Narrative, Analysis and Plans
2525 North Milwaukee
C2-2 District to B2-5 District (Type 1)

The Milshire Hotel LLC is the “Applicant” for a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment for the subject property
located at 2525 North Milwaukee Avenue from the C2-2 Motor Vehicle-Related Commercial District to the
B2-5 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District (Type 1) to redevelop the existing vacant 4-story building and allow
a change of use from single-room occupancy (SRO) to residential and mixed uses.

The site is located generally in the block bounded by West Logan Boulevard on the north, North Sacramento
Avenue on the east, and North Milwaukee Avenue on the south. The subject property consists of
approximately 5,361 square feet of site area and is improved with a vacant 4-story building constructed in
1928. The existing building contains approximately 18,358 square feet of floor area and was previously
operated as a SRO residential building known as The Milshire Hote! with 33 units. The former SRO ceased
operations in approximately 2015 and has remained vacant since that time. The building occupies
substantially all of the site and there are no off-street vehicular parking spaces. The property is a transit-
served location based on its proximity to the CTA Blue Line station entrance at Logan Square and the
Milwaukee Avenue bus line corridor.

The Applicant proposes to complete a historic rehabilitation of the existing building to upgrade aged and
substandard components of the structure and convert the 1st through 4th floors to multi-unit residential use.
The building will contain a total of 30 residential units (9 dwelling units and 21 efficiency units), including
ground-floor residential units. The ground floor will also contain approximately 1,225 square feet of ground-
floor commercial space. The building footprint will remain unchanged. The Applicant is seeking all relief
necessary, as allowed by the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, for the attached plans.

The Property is located within the Milwaukee Avenue Special Character Overlay District (the “MASCO
District”) and is designated as a character building within the district. The proposed rehabilitation is
consistent with the MASCO District Guidelines.
